name: Toilet Paper
tagline: Diagrams, Word documents and decks from a short source file.
summary: Turns YAML and Markdown into BPMN, flowcharts, RACI matrices, icon pictures, Word documents and decks. No language model inside.

hero.headline: Write a short source file. Get the diagram or the Word document.
hero.sub: Toilet Paper turns YAML and Markdown into BPMN, flowcharts, RACI matrices, icon pictures, Word documents and decks. There is no language model inside, so the same source gives the same output every time.

viewer.caption: A flowchart from {lines} lines. The source holds no coordinates: tp calculates the layout.

how.title: The agent writes the content. tp does the rest.
how.text: A source file says what is in the picture or the document. tp calculates the layout, draws it, stamps the output with the hash of its source and checks later that nothing published is older than its source.

agents.title: Built for agents to call
agents.text: The MCP server gives an agent eleven tools. Draft tools write a file only when the source is valid. When it is not, they return the full list of problems and write nothing.

tools.name: tp_schema
tools.text: The source format, with an example.

tools.text: Checks a source without rendering it.

tools.name: tp_render
tools.text: Makes the artifact.

tools.name: tp_draft_bpmn
tools.text: Takes YAML text. When it is valid, writes the file and renders it.

tools.name: tp_draft_raci
tools.text: Drafts a RACI source.

tools.name: tp_check
tools.text: Finds outputs older than their source.

tools.name: tp_preview
tools.text: Page images of a document, without opening Word.

tools.name: tp_import_bpmn
tools.text: Turns an existing diagram into a source.

tools.name: tp_icons
tools.text: Lucide icon names for a word.

tools.name: tp_variants
tools.text: Every variant and theme as PNG, to choose one.

tools.name: tp_audit
tools.text: Checks a Word file: header, footer, true file properties and the source stamp.

agents.snippet:
tp schema flow
tp render EXPENSE.flow.yaml
tp check ./docs
# exit 0: nothing to act on, 1: something to fix, 2: could not check

limits.title: The layout is automatic
limits.text: It avoids crossings and overlaps, but a person drawing by hand can make a tighter picture. The .bpmn opens in a modeler for polish, and a manual edit is lost on the next render.

limits.title: PDF needs Word
limits.text: The PDF comes from Microsoft Word, so the machine that renders needs it. Word also adds its own timestamps; the pages and text stay the same.

limits.title: Two helper apps are optional
limits.text: The sharpest PNG and the page preview use two small helper apps. Without them tp still renders, and says so.

limits.title: Old files are not judged
limits.text: A document made before tp shows as unstamped, never as stale, until it moves to a source file.

install.lead: Access is by request. The package installs offline on Windows, and an installed copy keeps itself current.

steps.title: Get the package
steps.text: It holds the tp wheel, the wheels of its libraries at the tested versions, install.ps1 and a SHA256SUMS file. It is shared on request, not published.

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.text: It makes a private Python environment, puts tp on your user PATH, registers the MCP server toilet-paper for Claude Code and copies a short skill. -Check only looks. -Uninstall removes everything.

steps.title: Updates
steps.text: An installed tp reads the VERSION of the folder it came from at most every 6 hours. When it is newer, it checks SHA256SUMS and updates itself. TP_NO_UPDATE=1 turns this off, and tp update --check shows the state. Releases are signed. tp status shows the installed version, and tp rollback goes back one version.
steps.code:
tp update --check
tp status
tp rollback

install.note: Working from source instead: pip install -e ".[dev,mcp,pdf]". PDF output needs Microsoft Word on the machine, and tp templates shows the Word template path it expects.

name: Vault Index
tagline: Find the right note by meaning, on your own machine.
summary: Hybrid search over a folder of Markdown notes, for people and for agents. No language model in the index, and nothing leaves the PC.

hero.headline: Find the right note by meaning, on your own machine.
hero.sub: Vault Index turns a folder of Markdown notes into a search index. It matches the words you typed and the meaning you meant, and returns the five best passages instead of every file that mentions your words. No model calls, and nothing leaves the PC.
hero.command: python -m vaultindex search "why did we stop the weekly status mail"

proof.label: faster than scanning every note, full-text mode
proof.note: Full-text mode: 0.09 s against 1.2 s for a keyword scan of 2,646 notes on 2026-10-20. Warm cache, one laptop.
proof.short: faster than a scan, full-text mode

proof.label: less text for the agent to read
proof.note: 5 passages, about 3,500 characters in all, against the 24 to 224 whole files a keyword search matched (1.1 to 4.7 million characters). About 900 tokens instead of 270,000 or more.

proof.label: of real questions answered in the top 5
proof.note: Hybrid search on 38 real questions, against 61% for full-text alone. Measured on 2026-09-03, before query translation was added.

proof.label: model calls per search
proof.note: No language model at any step. The only download is the embedding model, once, checked by hash. An optional local model can translate a query before it searches.

viewer_lead: A real run on an example vault of 12 notes. The command on the left, the output on the right, trimmed to the fields that matter.

viewer.caption: The question shares few words with the note title. The top result was found by full text, by meaning and by a link from another note.
Notes about people are indexed but left out by default. The answer says how many it left out, so a missing result does not look like a missing note.
The index is derived. check rehashes the notes and compares them with the index, and you can delete the index and rebuild it at any time.

how.title: Two searches, fused by rank.
how.text: Your notes stay the source of truth. The index is a single SQLite file next to them that you can delete and rebuild.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Reads every Markdown note, cuts it into passages of up to 600 characters and stores them. A rebuild skips every note that did not change.

steps.title: Embed
steps.text: A small model that runs on the CPU, inside the process, turns each passage into 384 numbers.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Full-text and vector results are fused by rank. A note linked from a better result moves up a little, and decisions weigh slightly above daily notes.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: check rehashes the notes and tells you if the index drifted from the files.

tables.title: Against scanning every file
tables.lead: Same 8 questions, same 2,646 notes. Hybrid trades speed for meaning, so it is slower than a scan on this machine.

Full-text mode
Hybrid mode

agents.title: Built for agents to call
agents.text: An MCP server exposes search and the session briefing. It loads the model once and keeps it for as long as the server runs. If the libraries are missing it falls back to a subprocess and says which path it used.

tools.name: vault_search
tools.text: Hybrid search with filters for type, folder and dates. Notes about people stay out unless asked.

tools.name: vault_briefing
tools.text: Opens a session from what is already written: the last session, open items, recent decisions. No model.

agents.snippet:
python -m vaultindex build --embed
python -m vaultindex search "retention for call notes" -k 5
python -m vaultindex check

limits.title: Hybrid search is not instant
limits.text: From the command line a cold hybrid search takes 12 to 16 s while the model loads. Warm, we measured 1.8 s on a busy laptop. Use --streams fts when speed matters.

limits.title: Ranking is not perfect
limits.text: The right note comes first for 29% of questions and in the top 5 for 76%. Treat the list as candidates.

limits.title: Markdown only
limits.text: It indexes .md files. Other formats are not read.

limits.title: People notes depend on a list
limits.text: The folders and note types treated as sensitive come from one list in the code. A note about a person outside those folders, with no listed type, is not filtered.

limits.title: New notes wait for vectors
limits.text: A search refreshes full-text before it answers, but vectors for new notes arrive with the daily 18:00 build. The answer says how many passages still lack them.

limits.title: It uses memory
limits.text: The MCP server with the model loaded holds about 520 MB of RAM while it runs.

method: Measured on 2026-10-20 on one Windows laptop, against a notes vault of 2,646 Markdown files (about 19 million characters). Scan: read every file and keep the ones that contain all the query words. Index: the same 8 queries through the search function in a running process. Medians, warm disk cache. Tokens are estimated at 4 characters each. The top-5 numbers come from the project benchmark of 38 real questions, run on 2026-09-03. Your numbers will differ with your notes and your machine.

impact.label: less text for the agent to read
impact.basis: 5 passages, about 3,500 characters in all against the 24 to 224 whole files a keyword search returns.

name: Vault Sources
summary: Brings videos and articles into your notes as sourced files, ranks what to watch against your own open questions, and proposes concept updates that only an explicit accept applies.

hero.headline: Bring outside knowledge into your notes, with its source attached.
hero.sub: Vault Sources fetches a video or an article with one command and writes a note that says where the text came from, when, and which question made you save it. A watchlist ranks new videos against what you are trying to learn. Nothing changes your notes until you accept it.
hero.command: python -m vaultsources fetch "<video url>" --question "why this matters"

proof.label: notes from outside the vault
proof.note: On 2026-09-10 the vault had 1,129 notes and none from outside. Today it has 35 source notes.
proof.source: docs/vaultsources.md, section What it is; assets/measurements.md

proof.label: sources already analysed
proof.note: A source starts as pending and stays visible until it is read.

proof.label: automatic consistency checks
proof.note: Broken references, missing folders, stale notes, hash mismatches and more, run by one command.

proof.label: paid APIs to fetch and transcribe
proof.note: yt-dlp, the platform captions and a local Whisper model.

viewer_lead: A real run in a scratch vault, with a public video. The command on the left, what it wrote or answered on the right.

viewer.caption: The note starts with provenance written by code: URL, author, date, how the text arrived, a hash of the text and the question that pulled it in. The analysis stays pending.
Fetching the same video again is refused unless you pass --force, and the list shows what still waits for a reading. The messages are in Portuguese.

how.title: One pipe, four steps.
how.text: Fetching, scoring and checking are code. Reading and judging a source is a separate step you run on purpose.

steps.title: Fetch
steps.text: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Vimeo, X and web articles. A transcript longer than 4,000 characters goes to a sidecar file so the note stays readable.

steps.title: Record provenance
steps.text: Code writes the source, the date, the way the text arrived and a hash of it. A check later notices if the text no longer matches.

steps.title: Analyse
steps.text: A session reads the text without timestamps, which are about 15% of a caption, and fills in the thesis, the claims with their source and what changes in your notes.

steps.title: Propose, never apply
steps.text: A change to a concept becomes a proposal. Only an explicit accept applies it, and a discard goes to a rejected folder instead of disappearing.

tables.title: One writer for every file
tables.lead: No state file is edited by hand. Each has one command that writes it.

Written by

tables.title: How a new video is ranked
tables.lead: The score is deterministic and explains itself. It matches the title against your open questions, not against a generic idea of relevance.

agents.title: Built to be driven by an agent
agents.text: Every step is a command with plain arguments and one writer, so an agent can run the whole pipe and a person can read what it did.

tools.name: fetch
tools.text: Brings one source in, with the question that pulled it.

tools.name: watch, poll, queue
tools.text: Subscribe to channels and playlists, score new videos, approve candidates.

tools.name: analyse
tools.text: Lists what waits for a reading, shows the text, applies the analysis.

tools.name: concept
tools.text: Creates, proposes, accepts or rejects a position in the concepts layer.

tools.name: qa
tools.text: Nine checks on the notes and the documents that describe them.

agents.snippet:
python -m vaultsources fetch "<url>" --question "why this matters"
python -m vaultsources analyse --list
python -m vaultsources qa --all

limits.title: LinkedIn cannot be fetched
limits.text: There is no open API, and scraping a logged-in page breaks with every release. The clip command takes the text from the session that read the page.

limits.title: Analysis needs a model session
limits.text: Fetching, scoring and checking are code. Reading a source and judging it is done by a Claude session you run, so it is not free of model calls.

limits.title: The ranking only knows what you wrote
limits.text: A subject that is not in your notes ranks by the feed topic alone, never by focus.

limits.title: Messages are in Portuguese
limits.text: Command output and note headings are in Portuguese. The front matter keys are in English.

limits.title: Some networks need setup
limits.text: yt-dlp must be the Python module, and a network that inspects TLS needs a CA bundle or every fetch fails with a certificate error.

method: Counts taken on 2026-10-20, read-only, from the owner's own notes vault: 35 source notes, 24 transcript files, 34 analysed and 1 pending. The 0-to-35 comparison uses the 2026-09-10 state from the project documentation. The demo is a real run on a public video in an empty scratch vault.

name: Capy
tagline: Every AI session in one window, with the cost in view.
summary: A desktop app that keeps Claude Code, Codex and Gemini sessions together, keeps API and plan accounts apart, checks every file write and shows what your key spends.

hero.headline: All your AI sessions in one window, with the cost in view.
hero.sub: Capy keeps your Claude Code, Codex and Gemini sessions together on your PC. It keeps API and plan accounts apart, checks every file write before it happens, shows what your key spends and writes the end-of-session note for you.

proof.label: cheaper to draft from a written note
proof.note: A measured draft went from $0.061 to $0.010 when drafts moved to a smaller model. Summaries and wrap-up notes stay on the larger one.

proof.label: unsafe actions blocked before any write
proof.note: A key or token written into a file, code fetched and run at once, TLS turned off, a changed execution policy and the deletion of a whole home folder.

proof.label: accounts that never mix
proof.note: API runs on your company key, Plan on your own subscription. Capy refuses a Plan message in a work folder or one that mentions work.

proof.label: releases in 8 days
proof.note: From 1.0.0 on 2026-10-16 to 1.26.4 on 2026-10-23. Help lists every version and what it changed.

screens_lead: Real screens from a fresh copy with no sessions, so nothing on them is anyone's work.

screens.caption: The home screen. Pick the account, the tool and the folder, or start from a template. Read only is on by default.
Start with a template: pick the task, fill in a few lines and Capy writes the message. You read it and press Send.

how.title: From a first message to a clean next session.
how.text: Capy follows the life of a conversation, not only its start.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Begin from a template or a blank chat. Pick the tool and the folder first. The AI reads the folder and changes nothing until you allow it.

steps.title: Work
steps.text: Turn on Can change files and every write is checked first. A command, such as the tests, shows with Allow and Don't allow and runs only after you click. Undo this reply puts back what a Claude Code reply changed. Review changes shows each file as a line diff: comment on any change and send all comments in one message, or put one change back.

steps.title: Wrap up
steps.text: Writes an end-of-session note: what happened, the decisions and the next steps, saved in your own vault. You can close the window while it is written.

steps.title: Continue clean
steps.text: Starts a new conversation that carries only the note. The old messages stay in the old session, and replies cost less and stay on track.

name: AI Spend View
tagline: Each person sees their monthly AI spend.
summary: Shows each person their monthly spend on an AI gateway, from a daily capture. The numbers stay on your PC and in your profile folder.

hero.headline: See what your AI key spent this month, without asking anyone.
hero.sub: AI Spend View reads your own key on the AI gateway twice a day and keeps the readings on your PC. A local page turns them into the spend since the 1st, a forecast for month end and a warning before you reach the limit you set.

proof.label: reads a day, plus one at startup
proof.note: A scheduled task reads the gateway at 09:00 and 17:00, and when the PC starts if a time passed while it was off.

proof.label: is the longest gap for an exact month
proof.note: The month figure is exact when a reading exists up to 3 days before the 1st or on the 1st. With the daily capture there is always one. Without it the page shows a range and marks it incomplete.
proof.source: README, section O que faz; CHANGELOG, version 1.3

proof.label: warnings a month, one at each mark
proof.note: A Windows notice at 80% and another at 100% of the limit you entered, once each per month.

proof.label: team-level calls an ordinary key cannot make
proof.note: User, team, key-list and spend-log queries return 403 for a normal key. The page therefore shows your own spend and nobody else's.

how.title: Read twice a day, compute on your PC.
how.text: The gateway reports one running total per key. It does not report the month. The page computes the month from your own readings, and says how sure it is.

steps.title: Install once
steps.text: Run the installer. It stores your key encrypted for your Windows user, asks for your monthly limit, creates the scheduled task and puts a shortcut on the desktop. No admin rights.

steps.title: Capture
steps.text: Each run reads the key total from the gateway and appends it to a history file in your own profile folder. It also refreshes the model price table.

steps.title: Compute
steps.text: The spend since the 1st is the sum of the rises between readings. A drop of more than 1 cent counts as a key reset. A smaller drop is rounding noise and counts as zero.

steps.title: Show and warn
steps.text: The local page shows the month spend against your limit, a month-end forecast and the price per model. Windows warns you at 80% and 100%, and when the gateway refuses the balance query.

tables.title: Two totals, two meanings
tables.lead: The page shows both so a key total above your limit does not look like an overrun.
head: Total on the key
Spend this month
rows: With a reading up to 3 days before the 1st

limits.title: Windows only
limits.text: The capture is a PowerShell task and the warnings are Windows notices.

limits.title: You enter your own limit
limits.text: The gateway does not report a monthly cap for a normal key. The page compares your spend with the number you typed at install, and says so when you left it blank.

limits.title: The month can be a range
limits.text: With no reading near the 1st, the page shows at least what rose since the first reading of the month and marks it incomplete. It never shows the whole key total as the month.

limits.title: No team view
limits.text: A normal key reads only its own total and the model list. Spend for a team needs the people who run the gateway.

limits.title: Opened files do not share a browser
limits.text: The page keeps manual readings in the browser. Another browser, or a localhost address, starts with its own empty store. The captured readings appear in all of them.

limits.title: No automated tests
limits.text: The tool has a change log and a manual check, but no test suite yet.

method: Statements come from the tool's own README and change log, and from reading its capture script. The two rules in the viewer were run on made-up numbers in a scratch folder. The capture itself was not run, because it calls the live gateway with a real key. The amounts are invented.
viewer_lead: The two rules that decide what the page shows, copied from the capture script with the comments translated, each run on made-up numbers in a scratch folder. The real capture needs a live gateway call with a real key, so it was not run.

viewer.caption: The gateway gives a running total. The month figure is the sum of rises between your readings, with a reset detected by a drop of more than 1 cent.
One notice per mark per month, against the limit you entered. With no limit entered, no notice fires.

name: Autodev
tagline: Free models build, Claude plans and reviews.
summary: An OpenCode model executes the task, Claude plans and reviews, and the tests are checked by mutation. Code waits for your ok. A team lead step caps how much work the free model gets.

hero.headline: Let a free model write the change. Check it with code, then with a review.
hero.sub: Autodev splits the work. Claude writes a task and reviews the result. A free model, run through OpenCode, makes the edits in an isolated worktree. A script checks scope, size, secrets and every test. Nothing is pushed without your ok. It runs on a personal project, with no company data and no company key.

proof.label: checks every task must pass
proof.note: The 26 tests and 4 validators that npm test runs, plus the task's own gate. The list is read from the main branch, so the model cannot shorten it.

proof.label: bad versions survived the last review
proof.note: Mutation review of the one task so far: 3 of 5 broken copies passed the test on attempt 1, 1 of 8 on attempt 2, none on attempt 3.
proof.source: docs/autodev.md, section Review that the gates cannot do

proof.label: lines in the one landed task
proof.note: A code change plus its test, produced by a free model in 156 seconds of executor time on the last attempt.

proof.label: retries at most
proof.note: A bounced task goes back with the reviewer's text. After the third attempt it goes to the owner.
proof.source: docs/autodev.md, section Review that the gates cannot do

proof.label: executor runs a day at most
proof.note: The team lead also caps attempts at 3 per task, open tasks at 1 and new tasks at 2 a week, and checks that a task fits before a run is spent.
proof.short: executor runs a day at most

viewer_lead: One task file in, one result record out. The task is an example; the result and the review numbers come from the one real run.

viewer.caption: A task names the files the model may edit, the gates it must pass and a size limit. The record keeps the exit code of every gate.
After the model stops, a script compares the changes with the task. A red result bounces the task and no review is spent.
The first task passed every machine check and its test still proved nothing. Breaking the code on purpose showed it.

how.title: Claude plans, a free model edits, code checks, Claude reviews.
how.text: Each step has one owner. The model that edits never decides whether its own work is good.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Claude reads the weekly report and the answer log, then writes one file per task. Only the task text goes to the free model, never the logs.

steps.title: Execute
steps.text: The runner resets an isolated worktree to main and runs the task with an OpenCode model. The default is a free one, and --model changes it.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: No model involved. Only allowed files changed, no forbidden path, the diff is under the limit, no secret in the added lines, and every check exits 0.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Claude reads the diff against the task in a clean session and breaks the changed code on purpose to see that the new test fails.

steps.title: Land
steps.text: land commits in the worktree and fast-forwards main. It never pushes. Deploy needs the owner's ok. A task that only adds new test files lands on its own, still without a push.

tables.title: What the executor can do
head: Allowed
rows: Any file except the runner, the task files, the deploy script, the test list, config, secrets, photos and the sync folder.
Everything except secrets, the sync folder, photos and the content banks. A hosted free model is assumed to log prompts, so that content stays with Claude.
Only node dev/test-*, node dev/validate-*, git status and git diff.
None. The web fetch and execute tools are denied.

tables.title: What the team lead allows
tables.lead: A step of the weekly routine plus a gate in the runner. No model is involved, and the executor cannot edit it.
head: Limit
Value
rows: 3, then it goes to the owner
2, only app scripts, test files, validators and the shared library
450 words at most, with an acceptance command and a named source

limits.title: A personal project only
limits.text: The free model is outside the company's approved AI. Autodev runs on a personal study app that holds no company data, and it never sees a company key.

limits.title: One task so far
limits.text: The page rests on a single landed task. It is not a success rate, and there is no measured saving against writing the change by hand.

limits.title: The lead's limits rest on one task
limits.text: They are a narrow start, not a measured throughput. They widen only after 10 landed tasks, and the first task would not pass them today: it allowed 200 lines.

limits.title: It tests logic, not screens
limits.text: A change to the interface needs a browser check by Claude before it lands.

limits.title: A green test can still be empty
limits.text: The first task passed every machine check with a test that proved nothing. Claude samples the auto-landed tests in a weekly pass.

limits.title: Setup is slow once
limits.text: Creating the isolated worktree took about 7 minutes in the app that uses it, because of its audio files. It happens once.

limits.title: Free model names change
limits.text: If a model disappears, pass --model. opencode-cli models lists what is available.

limits.title: It depends on one tool version
limits.text: The agent rules were worked out on OpenCode 2.0.30. A wrong form of one setting drops the whole agent file without a clear error.

name: Study Quest
tagline: A language-study game with a save state.
summary: Flashcards and battles over a study plan, with a save state. Study answers sync back to your notes vault.

hero.headline: A language-study game that goes easy on missed days.
hero.sub: Study Quest wraps a study plan in a map, flashcards and turn-based battles. Each answer is a move, a wrong one comes back as a rematch, and a missed week never leaves you stuck. Your answers flow to your own notes, and the game never writes there.

proof.label: checks behind every deploy
proof.note: One command runs all of them, and the deploy script and the CI workflow call the same list. All 30 passed on 2026-10-24.

proof.label: cases for the answer checker
proof.note: The checker decides if a typed answer is right, a small slip or wrong. The same code runs in battles, in practice and in the tests.

proof.label: HP, the most a missed stretch can cost
proof.note: The first missed day costs nothing. After that each day costs 10 HP up to 30, and you can still play at 0 HP.
proof.short: HP, the most a miss costs

proof.label: verbs, each with its own review box
proof.note: A correct answer moves a verb up a box and a wrong one moves it down. Boxes come back after 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days.

viewer_lead: Real runs of the project's own checks. They use an in-memory fake database, so nothing real is read or written.

viewer.caption: One command runs every check and prints the failures. A new test counts only once it is in that list.
The first fight with a guardian is at the lesson level. After you win, the rematch follows your level, with more HP and a stronger attack.
The server refuses a database whose label does not match the deployment. Tests and the dev server use a fake one.

how.title: Learn, fight, review.
how.text: The game state lives in the app. What you study flows one way, to your notes.

steps.title: Learn
steps.text: Every guardian on the map has a lesson first: a rule, examples with audio, the common mistake and a short check without HP loss. Fighting before the lesson asks you first.

steps.title: Fight
steps.text: Each question is a move: listen, grammar, read or speak. A move has 4 uses. A monster is weak to one type and resists another. A wrong answer returns as a rematch after 2 other questions.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Lines from lessons, nouns and verbs sit in review boxes with growing gaps. A weekly report counts answers by skill from the same log, with no model in between.

steps.title: Sync
steps.text: A script on your PC pulls answers and minutes from the app into your own tracker. The app never writes to your notes, and your notes never receive anything that did not pass through that script.

tables.title: How strict the checker is
tables.lead: A typo against a weak monster weakens the hit and costs no HP. Stronger monsters tolerate fewer slips.
head: Monster level
Strictness
Letters forgiven
Hit after a slip
Missing umlaut
rows: 1 up to 4 letters, 2 up to 10, else 3
1 for a word, 2 for a phrase, 3 for a long phrase
1, only in a phrase over 24 letters; a noun's capital letter counts

tables.title: Rules that keep it playable
head: Situation
What happens
rows: You faint, wake up with 50% HP and lose 10% of your coins. XP, items, streak and map stay.
It grows 10 per hour, even with the app closed.
The daily mission pays double XP and comes with a healing potion.
Never locked. The map shows the monster level and the level it recommends.
Three choices always. A test fails if the right answer is the longest too often.

tables.title: New since 2026-10-23
tables.lead: From the project's release notes, newest first.
head: Version
What it added
rows: A clean edition: one command builds the engine with one content pack, with no personal names, no photos and no work documents, and checks itself.
A content pack can bring its own title, greeting, class, ranks, move and monster names, and hide what only one language needs.
The engine asks the pack which language it teaches; a second pack, a small Mandarin demo with its own answer rules, runs on the same engine.
The content is written as YAML files, one lesson, place or character per file, and the code modules are generated from them.
The content tree written as YAML and read back byte for byte, with a schema for the slide types.

limits.title: Built for one player
limits.text: There is one account with one save per subject. The app is a personal build, not a product packaged for other people.

limits.title: You host it
limits.text: It needs a Vercel project and an Upstash Redis database. Sign-in is a passphrase of 12 characters or more, or a Google account on an allowed list.

limits.title: The state lives in one database
limits.text: Level, coins, items and the review schedule exist only there. The sync script keeps dated backups on your PC, and a restore needs a flag to run.

limits.title: Some check-ins are self-declared
limits.text: Minutes studied in another language app come from a tap, because that app has no official API.

limits.title: Rank is not a grade
limits.text: Level measures effort. Rank rises only on real milestones read from your tracker, and the mock exam inside the game does not replace a real one.

limits.title: Project notes are in Portuguese
limits.text: The README and the rules file are written in Portuguese. The interface comes in English, Portuguese and German, and English is the default.

method: Counts come from the project's own README, rules file and tests, and from running the test suite once on 2026-10-21 against the in-memory fake database. The check list and demo outputs are real runs, trimmed to the lines shown. No screenshots are shown because the game screens carry personal content.

name: Team Knowledge Q&A
summary: A knowledge layer for a team: pages, search and answers with their source. Every page has an owner, a class and a link to where it came from.

hero.headline: Ask the team's pages. Get the answer and the page it came from.
hero.sub: Team Knowledge Q&A keeps a team's decisions, lessons and how-tos as pages in tables on a hosted data platform. People and agents search them and ask questions. Every answer lists the pages behind it, and a question with no page behind it becomes a gap that someone can take.

proof.label: automated tests pass
proof.note: They cover permissions, versions, the answer path, the agent interface and the vault import. Each test builds its own temporary store.

proof.label: of 20 test questions found the right page in the top 5
proof.note: Vector search on the project's own questions, against 30% for the keyword search the app uses today. Questions were written from pages chosen first, so real questions will score lower.

proof.label: tools for agents over MCP
proof.note: Search pages, get a page, list gaps, report a gap and a review summary. They follow the same visibility rules as the screens.

proof.label: API routes behind the screens
proof.note: Pages, versions, search, ask, comments, gaps and decisions. A page can be read, saved and restored without the screens.

viewer_lead: Real requests to the app running in a scratch folder with 2 invented pages. The request on the left, the response on the right, trimmed to the fields that matter.

viewer.caption: The answer lists the page it used with its owner, status and whether anyone verified it. No language model was attached in this run, so the app returned the sources without prose. With a model attached, the answer cites them as [1], [2].
A question that matches no page comes back as unanswered instead of a guess. The app can turn it into a gap page for an owner to take.
A page without a source link is refused. Text about a person's pay, health, identity or a credential is refused with no override.

how.title: A page in, an answer out, and a gap when nothing fits.
how.text: Pages live in tables. A small FastAPI app serves the screens, the API and an MCP endpoint from the same code.

steps.title: Write
steps.text: A page has a type, an owner, a classification, a source link and a review date. Every save is a new version, with a diff against the last one.

steps.title: Keep
steps.text: Verified pages carry a badge with a review date. Changing the title or the text removes the badge. Two people saving at once get a conflict, not a silent overwrite.

steps.title: Ask
steps.text: Search finds pages by keyword, with typo correction. Ask returns the pages it used, and an attached model writes the answer from them. Restricted pages never enter search or answers.

steps.title: Close the gap
steps.text: A question with no page becomes a gap page. Anyone can take it, and nobody else can take it once it is taken.

tables.title: Rules the app enforces
tables.lead: Each rule has a test in the project.
head: Rule
What happens
rows: The save is refused unless the source is a link or a known reference.
Hard groups are refused. Softer groups, such as a promotion stage, need the author to confirm once.
Visible to the owner, the space owner and the author. Never in search, answers or the agent interface for anyone else.
Created by the owners of the app. Anyone can create a topic space.

tables.title: Page types
head: Group
Types

agent-charter, agent-sources, agent-autonomy, agent-rules, agent-runbook, agent-handoff

agents.title: Built for agents to call
agents.text: An MCP endpoint and a small API let an agent look things up and report what is missing. Callers sign in with the platform, and a script or agent can use a service identity.

tools.name: search_pages
tools.text: Search with the same visibility rules as the screens.

tools.name: get_page
tools.text: Read one page, if the caller may see it.

tools.name: list_gaps
tools.text: List the questions that no page answers.

tools.name: report_gap
tools.text: Record a question as a gap that nobody has taken.

tools.name: review_summary
tools.text: Titles and links of pages due for review, with no page text.

limits.title: Search is keyword-only until the index exists
limits.text: The vector index needs a schema and a scheduled job that are not in place. Until then the app finds pages by keyword, which put the right page in the top 5 for 30% of the 20 test questions.

limits.title: Data is lost on redeploy without the tables
limits.text: Without the schema and its grants, the app falls back to a SQLite file that resets on every deploy or restart.

limits.title: The answer needs an attached model
limits.text: Without one, the app returns the sources and no written answer.

limits.title: The agent interface is not proven yet
limits.text: The MCP endpoint passes its tests. A first connection from a real agent builder has not been tried.

limits.title: The eval is small
limits.text: 20 questions in one language, each written from a page chosen first. Treat 90% as an upper bound.

limits.title: Bound to one platform
limits.text: Storage, identity and the index use the hosted data platform. A local SQLite mode exists for development only.

name: Team Memory Agent
runs: Windows scheduled tasks, private lake in OneDrive
tagline: Daily meetings become a weekly record.
summary: Captures every hour and consolidates by code. A week becomes record only after you approve it.

hero.headline: Daily meetings become a weekly record, and you approve it first.
hero.sub: Team Memory Agent captures a team's daily meeting records every hour and writes one weekly draft. Plain code does the merge, so every line traces to a dated source. The week enters the record only after its owner reads it and says yes.

proof.label: models in the merge
proof.note: Consolidation and publication are deterministic code. Models write the meeting summaries upstream and translate titles locally, and the docs say so.
proof.source: GOVERNANCE.md, rule No model in the merge

proof.label: sensitive-content patterns
proof.note: English and Portuguese patterns for health, pay and dismissal flag a draft. The list helps the reader. The reader is the gate.

proof.label: tests, on synthetic data
proof.note: They cover the raw layer, the consent rule, the deterministic rebuild and the guard against the real data. Capture is not covered.

proof.label: to sync when nothing has changed
proof.note: Each layer is rebuilt only when its inputs changed, checked by a hash. Recorded in the project README on 2026-10-07.

viewer_lead: What is real here: the test names, the reviewer checklist and the layout, taken from the product files. None of it is a run on meeting data.

viewer.caption: The first command validates the draft and prints what a machine cannot check. The second writes the week to the record, and only the owner runs it.
Originals are never edited. Everything above them is rebuilt from them, and queries run in memory so a synced database file cannot corrupt.
The names are the specification: append-only originals, a recording marked no-consent never enters, and a guard that refuses to run tests against real data.

how.title: Capture, consolidate, approve.
how.text: Each layer reads only the one before it. The only step a person owns is the last one.

steps.title: Capture
steps.text: Every hour it reads new meeting summaries and writes one immutable daily record per meeting.

steps.title: Consolidate
steps.text: On Fridays deterministic code turns the daily records into one weekly draft. Reruns are byte-identical, and contradictions are shown, not resolved.

steps.title: Approve
steps.text: The owner reads the draft and deletes what should not be there. The sensitive-content check runs on the edited text, so deleting a passage clears its flag.

steps.title: Keep
steps.text: An approved week is stored in the record. Nothing publishes to a shared library on its own, and the approved copy is kept because no rebuild can recreate a human decision.

tables.title: Scheduled tasks
head: Task
Runs
Does
rows: Reads new sources, writes daily records, syncs the lake
Fetches the meeting recaps and keeps a raw copy
Consolidates on Fridays and files away weeks the owner approved
Reads each task's last result and every lake run, then sends an alert on a failure

tables.title: What the validator refuses
tables.lead: Deterministic checks only. Rules a machine cannot check are printed as a checklist, never marked as passed.
head: Check
Result if it fails
rows: Status is not draft, or the week does not match the filename
One of 7 required headings is missing
No dated source listed, or a source count of zero
Flag, cleared by editing the text or by stating a reason

limits.title: One owner
limits.text: It is built for one person and one machine. There is no multi-user review flow.

limits.title: Approval is manual
limits.text: The quality of the record depends on the reader. The pattern list is a helper and misses what it does not name.

limits.title: Quiet days stay empty
limits.text: A day with only a transcript carries no notes, decisions or actions until someone writes them in or a summary arrives.

limits.title: Recaps depend on the source
limits.text: If the source tool generates no summary that day, there is nothing to capture, and the agent cannot tell why.

limits.title: Tests cover the lake
limits.text: The 10 tests run on synthetic data and cover the storage layer and the series title. Capture and consolidation have no automated test.

limits.title: Nothing is exposed as a service
limits.text: It runs as scheduled tasks and a command line. There is no screen to open.

name: Vault MCP
tagline: Let Claude read and write your notes vault, on your own machine.
summary: An MCP server for the backlog, daily logs and briefs of a notes vault. 13 tools, no model inside, nothing leaves the PC.

hero.headline: Let Claude read and write your notes vault.
hero.sub: Vault MCP gives an assistant 13 tools over a folder of Markdown notes: the backlog, the daily notes, weekly briefs, agent reports and session logs, plus search and a session briefing. Inputs are checked against fixed lists first, and every write is logged in the day's note. It runs over stdio on your PC and has no language model inside.

proof.label: tools in one server
proof.note: 10 read, 3 write. 44 parameters in all, 1 to 10 per tool.

proof.label: tools that can change a file
proof.note: They create an idea, update an idea and tick a to-do. The other 10 are marked read-only.

proof.label: writes leave a line in the daily note
proof.note: Create, update and to-do each added one entry to the day's note in the demo run.

proof.label: language model calls inside the server
proof.note: Tools read and write files and call the Vault Index search. Search uses a small embedding model through the Vault Index. The assistant that calls the tools is the only language model.

viewer_lead: Real calls against an invented vault of 3 notes, made from the tool functions. Each call on the left, the answer on the right, trimmed to the fields that matter.

viewer.caption: The list is a compact summary with paging. A full idea, with description, to-dos and notes, comes from a separate call.
An update changes only the fields you pass. Each write adds a line to the day's note, so the history of what the assistant changed is one read away.
Status, priority, area and effort are fixed lists. A value outside the list fails before any file is opened.
The cross-reference call skips notes about people unless you ask. The answer says it skipped them, so silence is not read as no mention.

how.title: A thin layer over files you already have.
how.text: The notes stay the source of truth. The server holds no database and no copy of them.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: An MCP client launches the server as a subprocess and talks to it over stdio. There is no network port. One environment variable points it at the vault.

steps.title: Validate
steps.text: Each tool takes a typed input. Unknown fields, bad dates and values outside the fixed lists are rejected before any file is touched.

steps.title: Read and write
steps.text: Ideas are Markdown files with a frontmatter block. A write rewrites only the fields it was given and keeps the rest of the file as it was.

steps.title: Log
steps.text: Every write appends one line to the backlog section of the day's note. Search and the briefing hand off to the Vault Index, in process when its libraries are installed and through a subprocess when they are not.

tables.title: What it exposes
tables.lead: 13 tools. Only the ones marked write change a file.
head: Tool
What it does
Access
rows: Lists ideas, filtered by status, area or priority, with paging.
Returns one idea in full: fields, description, to-dos, notes.
Creates the next idea file and logs it in the day's note.
Changes status, priority, impact, effort or due date, or appends a note. Logs it.
Ticks or reopens one to-do, matched by a substring. Several matches return an error that lists them.
Returns the day's note, which carries the backlog activity log.
Returns the weekly brief, the latest one by default.
Returns the report a scheduled job wrote for one day.
Returns the session log for one day.
Collects every mention of one idea across daily, report and session files.
Returns the one-to-one notes of one person. The only tool built for people notes.
Hybrid search of the vault through the Vault Index, with filters. People notes are out unless asked.
Opens a session from what is already written: last session, open items, recent decisions.

limits.title: One person, one machine
limits.text: The server runs over stdio for a single user and has no sign-in. Whoever can start it can read what its tools can read.

limits.title: The vault layout is fixed
limits.text: Folder names, note formats and the lists of statuses and areas are written in the code. Another vault needs code changes first.

limits.title: Writes have no undo
limits.text: Create takes the next free id and update appends its note each time it runs. Rolling back relies on the vault's own history.

limits.title: Context misses current daily notes
limits.text: vault_get_context_for_idea reads the old diary folder for daily entries. In the demo it found nothing for an idea the day's note had just logged.

limits.title: People notes come back whole
limits.text: vault_list_one_on_ones returns every matching note in full and does not page, so one call can be large.

limits.title: No automated tests yet
limits.text: The repo has no test suite. The tools were exercised by hand over stdio. Treat a first run on a real vault with care.

limits.title: Status names are in Portuguese
limits.text: Backlog statuses and the log tags the server writes are in Portuguese.

method: Counts come from importing the server module and listing its registered tools on 2026-10-20. The demo calls ran in process against an invented vault of 3 notes in a scratch folder; nothing was read from or written to a real vault. Search and briefing figures belong to the Vault Index page and were not repeated here.

install.lead: A local MCP server. It needs Python 3.10 or later and a virtual environment of its own.

steps.title: Make a dedicated environment and install
steps.text: The server needs mcp below version 2: version 2 renamed FastMCP, and the import breaks. A separate environment also keeps other tools' dependency conflicts out.

steps.title: Point it at your vault
steps.text: If the vault is not in the default path, set the environment variable VAULT_ROOT to its root folder. It goes in the env block of the registration below. The search and briefing tools also need the Vault Index code on the same PC.

steps.title: Try it before you rely on it
steps.text: The MCP inspector opens a local page where you can call each tool by hand.
steps.code:
python -m py_compile server.py vault_io.py
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector python server.py

steps.title: Register it in your MCP client
steps.text: Add the server to the client's JSON config with the environment's python.exe as the command, server.py as the argument and VAULT_ROOT in env. Close the client before you edit its config, then restart it.

install.note: Without onnxruntime, tokenizers and numpy in the environment, search falls back to a slower subprocess and says so in the bridge field.
install.source: README of the vault-mcp repository, sections on install, testing and registering

backlog.title: Multi-call search, measured against the one-shot search
